/-!
# Conjecture 2.84

by V. P. Shunkov

Suppose that a locally finite group $G$ is a product of two locally nilpotent
subgroups. Is $G$ necessarily locally soluble?

A group is *locally finite* (resp. *locally nilpotent*, *locally soluble*) if every
finitely generated subgroup is finite (resp. nilpotent, soluble). "Soluble" is the
British spelling of "solvable". The group $G$ is the *product* $G = AB$ of its subgroups
$A$ and $B$ if every element of $G$ can be written as $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$;
the subgroups $A$ and $B$ need not be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, universally quantified over all locally finite groups G and pairs of locally nilpotent subgroups A, B with G = AB as a set product (A, B need not be normal, and 'product' is the setwise product {ab}, not the join); 'locally finite/nilpotent/soluble' mean every finitely generated subgroup is finite/nilpotent/soluble, definitions which are not in Mathlib and must be introduced (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G A B, ... → locally soluble G).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same theorem: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G), IsLocallyFinite G → IsLocallyNilpotent A → IsLocallyNilpotent B → (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ → IsLocallySolvable G, with 'locally P' = every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is P (c02 uses the equivalent 'closure of every finite set is P'). The product is the setwise pointwise product (verified to unfold to ∀ g, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a*b = g), no normality is imposed, and the hypotheses are satisfiable (A = ⊤, B = ⊥), so the statement is non-vacuous and answer(True) is the affirmative answer. c03 chosen as base: universe-polymorphic bespoke definitions with explicit G, implicit G in the four proved API lemmas (Mathlib style), Mathlib-consistent name IsLocallySolvable, thorough docstrings, and G : Type in the theorem following the Kourovka/ directory idiom (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76). Only cosmetic docstring edits made.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.84

by V. P. Shunkov

Suppose that a locally finite group $G$ is a product of two locally nilpotent
subgroups. Is $G$ necessarily locally soluble?

A group is *locally finite* (resp. *locally nilpotent*, *locally soluble*) if every
finitely generated subgroup is finite (resp. nilpotent, soluble). "Soluble" is the
British spelling of "solvable". The group $G$ is the *product* $G = AB$ of its subgroups
$A$ and $B$ if every element of $G$ can be written as $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$;
the subgroups $A$ and $B$ need not be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«2.84»

/-- A group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group is *locally soluble* (locally solvable) if every finitely generated subgroup is
soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A soluble group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable [IsSolvable G] : IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally nilpotent group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.isLocallySolvable (h : IsLocallyNilpotent G) :
    IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun H hH => haveI := h H hH; inferInstance

/--
Suppose that a locally finite group $G$ is a product of two locally nilpotent
subgroups. Is $G$ necessarily locally soluble?

Here $G = AB$ is the setwise product $\{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ of the
subgroups $A$ and $B$, which are not assumed to be normal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.84» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsLocallyFinite G → IsLocallyNilpotent A → IsLocallyNilpotent B →
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      IsLocallySolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.84»

items: 'Locally P' is formalized as 'every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is P'. This agrees with the alternative convention 'every finite subset is contained in a P-subgroup' because finiteness, nilpotency and solvability are all subgroup-closed.

'G is a product of two locally nilpotent subgroups' is formalized as A B : Subgroup G with (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ (pointwise product of sets, i.e. every g = a*b with a ∈ A, b ∈ B). Verified in a scratch check that this unfolds to ∀ g, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a * b = g. A and B are not assumed normal, and the product is not the join.
Local nilpotency of the subgroups is stated for the coerced group types ↥A and ↥B (IsLocallyNilpotent A means every f.g. subgroup of A, as a group, is nilpotent).
G is quantified over Type (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76); the bespoke definitions themselves are universe-polymorphic.
'Soluble' is rendered via Mathlib's IsSolvable; the bespoke predicate is named IsLocallySolvable to follow Mathlib naming.

Four short, fully proved @[category API] lemmas were added as basic tests of the new definitions (finite ⇒ locally finite, nilpotent ⇒ locally nilpotent, solvable ⇒ locally solvable, locally nilpotent ⇒ locally solvable).

Definitions were kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, since the task restricts writes to the single candidate file; a reviewer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as reusable definitions.

reviewer_notes: Statement is unambiguous; no candidate omitted the slot. Points a reviewer may want to know: (1) 'locally P' is formalized as 'every f.g. subgroup is P'; this agrees with the alternative textbook convention 'every finite subset lies in a P-subgroup' because finiteness, nilpotency and solubility are subgroup-closed. (2) Local nilpotency of A, B is asserted for the coerced group types ↥A, ↥B, which is equivalent to asking that every f.g. subgroup of G contained in A (resp. B) is nilpotent. (3) G is quantified over Type (universe 0) per the repository's Kourovka idiom; this loses no generality since a counterexample in any universe yields a countable one (take the closure of a f.g. non-soluble subgroup under the factorization). (4) Bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) since the pipeline produces a single file; a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/GroupTheory. c06's use of Type* in the theorem statement is also fine but deviates from the directory idiom; c02's closure-based definitions are equivalent.
